property_summary: The invariant that pastBlockTime never stays the same after a call with msg.value == 10 ether is satisfied by the original contract but broken by the mutant.
When a call with msg.value == 10 ether reverts due to timestamp not strictly greater than pastBlockTime, the original contract does not update pastBlockTime, while the mutant does.
After any successful call with msg.value == 10 ether, the stored pastBlockTime is strictly greater than the block timestamp at the start of the call.
pastBlockTime is always strictly greater than the last block timestamp on entry
After any transaction with msg.value == 10 ether, pastBlockTime is strictly greater than the block timestamp when the transaction started.
After any call to the fallback function with exactly 10 ether, pastBlockTime increases by exactly 1.
After any call to the fallback function with exactly 10 ether, the value of pastBlockTime is exactly block.timestamp + 1.
After a successful fallback call with exactly 10 ether, pastBlockTime is set to block.timestamp + 1.
After any fallback call, the state variable pastBlockTime is updated to at least block.timestamp + 1.

When sending exactly 10 ether, the fallback must revert (require(msg.value == 10 ether) ensures no ether is ever transferred out on the first call if caller sends exactly 10 ether, but with > the caller can succeed and then later get a transfer).
After any sequence of calls, the contract's balance must never be reduced below 10 ether when accumulate function is not called.
After any sequence of state-changing calls where the message value is always exactly 10 ether, the contract's balance never decreases.
After sending exactly 10 ether via the fallback, the contract balance never decreases as a result of that call.
After any call to the fallback with value of exactly 10 ether, the contract balance must not decrease.
After any call to the fallback function, the contract's balance remains unchanged if it was not exactly 10 ether; the reference requires exactly 10 ether, the mutant allows less.
After any sequence of calls ending with a successful fallback call, the contract will revert on the next fallback call if the block timestamp has not advanced.
After calling fallback with 10 ether, the new pastBlockTime must be strictly greater than the block timestamp at the start of the call.
After a successful fallback call with 10 ether, pastBlockTime must be greater than the block timestamp when the call was made.
After a call to fallback that does not revert and block.number % 15 != 0, pastBlockTime must be strictly greater than the block timestamp at the time of the call.
The contract C should not allow two different callers to both receive the balance transfer in the same block when the block number is a multiple of 15.

The fallback function should not allow two calls from different addresses in the same block if block.number % 15 == 0, because the balance is transferred to the first caller, leaving the second with no balance to receive.
After a call that triggers the fallback, the updated pastBlockTime must be strictly greater than the current block timestamp.
After any call to fallback, the contract balance remains zero if block number meets the condition, else remains unchanged.
After a successful fallback call that does not trigger balance transfer due to block number condition, the contract balance increases by exactly 10 ether.

After a successful fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether, the contract's balance should always be zero when block.number % 15 == 0, but the mutant's condition (block.number % 15 == 1) allows the balance to remain non-zero.
After any fallback call with exactly 10 ether, the contract balance should be zero if the block number is divisible by 15.
